one_sentence: This document catalogs 36 structural isomorphisms between physics/mathematics and Christian theology, asserting that shared topological patterns across domains reveal a unified underlying reality.
executive_summary: The Isomorphism Registry presents 36 documented correspondences between physical/mathematical structures and Christian theological concepts, organized under the Theophysics Research Initiative. Each entry follows a standardized format: a core claim, a swap test for bidirectionality, confidence level, and falsification conditions. The registry spans domains from quantum mechanics (collapse ↔ Fall) to immunology (self/non-self ↔ sanctification) to music theory (harmonic series ↔ Trinity). High-confidence entries include the Trinity ↔ mathematical structure (ISO-001), grace ↔ impossibility theorems (ISO-002), and entropy ↔ sin (ISO-003). The document argues that these structural isomorphisms are not mere analogies but reflect a shared underlying reality, with the strongest mappings passing rigorous topological tests. The registry concludes that no entry has been falsified, though several remain at candidate or undetermined status.
short_summary: This document is the canonical registry of 36 structural isomorphisms between physics/mathematics and Christian theology. The core structural claim is that identical topological patterns—such as binary classification, sigmoidal dose-response, and three-mode temporal governance—appear independently in both domains. Key evidence includes high-confidence mappings like the Trinity ↔ mathematical structure (ISO-001), grace ↔ impossibility theorems (ISO-002), and addiction ↔ sin bondage (ISO-026), all of which pass bidirectional swap tests. This matters because it suggests a unified framework where theological claims are not merely metaphorical but structurally isomorphic to fundamental physical laws, with testable predictions and falsification conditions.
